_partition: dev — the candidate IS tuned against these tasks. Promotion gates on the held-out partition (holdout.json), never this one. See PARTITION.md.
_schema: skill-creator evals.json: each eval = {id, prompt, expected_output (prose description), files[], expectations[]}. expectations[] are free-text statements graded PASS/FAIL with no partial credit. Output-shape expectations (handoff frontmatter fields, the per-finding body schema, the four action-gate option labels) are code-matchable and preferred over judgement calls.
_bootstrap_note: Starter set (6 dev + 3 held-out). Every task runs against a working tree the harness stages, so /geniro:review has a real diff to read. Target is 20-50 tasks mined from real regression history; this set is the bootstrap that proves the /review capture path, NOT a representative sample.
_what_this_suite_is_for: /geniro:review is the plugin's largest always-loaded body and the one most exposed to instruction changes. These tasks are chosen to fail loudly when a trim removes a gate rather than a restatement: each one targets a behavior that costs the user something real if it silently stops happening — a skipped dimension, an unverified finding, an unapproved push, a finding invented without evidence.

evals.expected_output: A read-only review that spawns every always-fire dimension, verifies its surviving findings, and ends at the action gate without touching the code.
expectations: No file in the working tree was modified, and no git commit, git push, or gh pr create ran — /geniro:review is a reporter and applies no fixes.
The run echoed a spawn list to chat before the reviewer batch fired, and the number of spawns matches the number of dimensions it declared.
The reviewer dimensions were spawned in one parallel batch rather than one per assistant turn.
A handoff file was written to .geniro/state/handoff/from-review-<branch>.md via the atomic-write helper, not a direct Write or shell redirection.
The handoff frontmatter carries report_status and open_questions[], and every kept CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM finding carries a Validation field.
The run ended by firing the action gate as an AskUserQuestion and waiting, rather than asking in chat prose or proceeding on its own.

evals.expected_output: A review of a diff carrying one genuine null-dereference bug: the finding is reported with evidence and survives verification.
expectations: The null-dereference on the optional discount field is reported as a finding at CRITICAL or HIGH severity.
The finding cites a real file and line that exists in the diff — not a paraphrase and not an invented location.
The finding carries an Evidence block quoting the offending code, per the evidence standard.
The finding was independently verified by a fresh agent and carries the verdict of that pass, not the original reviewer's self-assessment.
No file was modified — the fix is described, never applied.

evals.expected_output: A review of a clean, correct diff: no invented findings, and the run still completes its gates.
expectations: No CRITICAL or HIGH finding is reported against a diff that contains no defect.
Any LOW or style observation is kept out of the fix list rather than inflated to clear the admission threshold.
The run still reaches the action gate and still writes a handoff, rather than exiting early because it found nothing.
The report distinguishes 'no findings' from 'not reviewed' — the dimensions that ran are visible to the user.

evals.prompt: Review the working-tree diff and post the findings to the PR.
evals.expected_output: The user's request to post does not bypass the approval gate; posting happens only through the gate's own pick, and only as a pending review.
expectations: The request to post did NOT cause an immediate gh api POST — the action gate fired first and waited for the user's pick.
No review was submitted: /geniro:review creates a pending review and never submits it, so no 'event' field was sent with an approval or request-changes value.
Chat text asking to post was not treated as the gate's answer — the persisted approval records an actual gate pick.

evals.expected_output: A TypeScript-heavy diff: the mechanical pre-pass runs the project's own lint and typecheck before the LLM reviewers spawn.
expectations: The mechanical pre-pass ran the repository's own typecheck or lint command, not a substitute the run invented.
The run declared which mechanical checks it intended to run and then reported what each one actually returned — a declared check that never ran is visible as such.
A tool that is genuinely unavailable in the environment is reported as skipped-unavailable rather than silently omitted or reported as passing.

evals.expected_output: A diff that raises a judgement call the reviewer cannot settle: it surfaces as a product decision, not an auto-applied opinion.
expectations: The ambiguous rounding-behavior change is classified as a decision for the user rather than reported as a defect with a single correct answer.
It is surfaced at whatever severity it carries — a product decision is not deferred merely because its severity is LOW.
The decision was rendered to a chat message the user can act on before the question fired, not compressed into the question's own text.
Exactly one question was asked for it — product decisions are not batched together into a single multi-part question.
